newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Solvay to sell animal health business.
newsitem.headline: Solvay to sell animal health business.

text.p: Belgian chemical group Solvay said in a statement on Friday it plans to sell all its animal health activities worldwide to American Home Products Corporation for an about $450 million (14 billion Belgian francs).

The transaction, which is subject to audits and final closing adjustments, would generate for the Solvay group a pretax capital gain estimated at $190 million (six billion Belgian francs), the company said.
The sale should be effective on December 31, 1996, subject to receipt of all necessary approvals and regulatory clearances.
The proceeds from the sale will be reinvested, through selective acquisitions of either pharmaceutical product lines or companies, especially in North America, Solvay said.
After the sale, Solvay will cease all its activities in the animal health business and focus on human health.
The health sector in 1995 represented 15 percent of Solvay's earnings before interest and taxes and had total sales of 44 billion Belgian francs.
American Home Products, based in New Jersey, U.S., is one of the world's largest research-based pharmaceutical and health care products companies.
Brussels-based Solvay is an international chemical and pharmaceutical group with operations in 44 countries. It employs more than 38,000 people.
